{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI Hosting / Site Development Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Contract review findings, walk-away items and next steps

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.2 against our playbook. The agreement is materially incomplete on risk allocation and materially one-sided on exit and exclusivity.

The most serious problems are omissions. There is **no IP or data ownership provision** at all, even though HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and data. There is **no limitation of liability** — no cap, no exclusion of consequential damages, no carve-out architecture — leaving both parties fully exposed. There is **no vendor indemnity**, **no vendor insurance**, **no performance warranty** (Section 9 carries only corporate-authority representations), and **no post-termination transition or data return mechanic**.

On the negotiated terms, the exit economics run against us. Section 4.2 imposes an uncapped Termination Payment on the Company whenever we terminate (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments), while Section 4.1 reads as an auto-renewal mechanic that lets HDI's notice fix any termination date — so HDI effectively holds a mid-term walk-away and we pay to leave. Section 6.1 binds us to full-term exclusive dealing on Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, with no performance-based exit, and hands HDI an exclusive right in our own "Deerskin" brand. Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited records inspection right. Section 10.5 selects New York law but fixes no forum.

Three rules are clean and require no redline: no Customer MFN, no minimum purchase or volume commitment (fees are a purely variable revenue share), and no non-solicitation covenant binding us. HDI's promotional "no less favorably" covenant in Section 1.8 and its reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 run in our favour and are untouched.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 | No IP or data ownership provision anywhere; only grant is the limited Section 6.1 trademark licence. Insert Company ownership of Site/deliverables and Company Data, HDI background IP with licence back, no joint ownership. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap, no consequential damages exclusion, no carve-outs. Insert mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 10.3 is binding-effect only: no consent standard, no affiliate/M&A carve-out, and HDI may assign to a competitor. Add assignment rights and consent standard. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6.1 imposes full-term exclusive dealing (auto-renewing under 4.1) with no service-level or delivery exit. Replace with express non-exclusivity; fallback is 12 months limited to Deerskin Products with automatic exit on failure. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 4.2 Termination Payment is uncapped and can far exceed three months' fees. Retain the calculation but cap at three months' Section 3.1 fees and confirm sole liquidated amount. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6.1 bars "substantially similar" products (open-ended) and gives HDI exclusivity in our own brand; no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Remove restriction and brand exclusivity. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 | No express Company convenience right; HDI's notice may fix any date; exit fee uncapped. Add 90-day Company convenience right, limit HDI to end of then-current term, cap Termination Payment at three months' Section 3 fees. |
| 8 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 3.4 already gives 30 days' notice with HDI bearing cost, but has no frequency limit (unlimited audits). Cap at once per year. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 10.5 selects New York law (preferred) but no forum, jurisdiction or arbitration provision exists. Add exclusive New York County venue, carve-out for temporary injunctive relief. |
| 10 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 1.4 grant runs to "the Company" only, with no affiliate coverage; successor element is met by Section 10.3. Extend access and use rights to affiliates on written notice. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 | No Customer MFN. The only "no less favorably" mechanic (§ 1.8) is an obligation on HDI running in our favour. Sits at the preferred position; no redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 | Fees are a purely variable 30% revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor (§§ 3.1–3.3); no minimum, take-or-pay or volume cap. Section 4.2 is an exit fee, addressed under the LD and T4C rules. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant anywhere; § 10.7 integration confirms none is imported. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal window | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 4.1 requires 90 days' notice to stop automatic one-year renewals, above the 60-day fallback ceiling. Shorten the Company's window to 60 days; HDI's 90 days retained. No renewal uplift mechanic exists, so the price-cap element is not engaged. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | Sections 4.1–4.2 address only notice and the Termination Payment; no migration help, return, export or deletion of Company Content or data. Insert new Section 4.3 (six months' assistance, 30-day data return, certified deletion). |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 9 contains only corporate-authority representations and the Globix acknowledgment; no conformance or services warranty and no remedy. Insert 90-day software conformance / 30-day services warranty with repair, replacement or refund. |
| 17 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere, despite HDI developing, hosting and operating the Site. Insert preferred-level HDI indemnity with standard procedure and a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company Content and our breach of law. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance covenant anywhere, though HDI processes Company data. Insert Section 10.9 (CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy, workers' compensation, certificates on request). |

All findings above have been verified. Three (LD, T4C, RENEWAL) were repaired during verification; the substance is as stated.

---

## Walk-away items

These sit at or beyond our walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiable trade-offs:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN).** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site. The complete absence of any HDI indemnity for third-party IP infringement or its own misconduct is walk-away territory, and it is compounded by the absence of any limitation-of-liability architecture.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** HDI hosts the Site on its own systems and has access to Company Content, user information and data. No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data is a walk-away.
3. **Unlimited audit frequency (AUDIT, § 3.4).** HDI may inspect our records repeatedly with no annual limit. The once-per-year cap is the minimum acceptable outcome.
4. **90-day non-renewal window (RENEWAL, § 4.1).** This sits at the walk-away threshold; 60 days for the Company is required.

We also flag, as commercially critical though not framed as walk-aways: the **missing IP/data ownership provision** and the **missing limitation of liability** — both critical omissions in a hosting arrangement — and the combination of **full-term exclusivity with no performance exit plus an uncapped exit fee** (§§ 6.1, 4.1, 4.2), which together leave us locked in with no priced route out.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering all fourteen deviation and missing items, with `[Playbook]` comments stating the position and the fallback where one is offered.
2. **Lead with the four omissions** (IP ownership, limitation of liability, indemnity, insurance) plus transition assistance and the performance warranty. These are new inserts rather than edits and should be tabled as a package before we trade on the negotiated terms.
3. **Negotiate the exit economics as one item.** The Section 4.2 cap at three months' Section 3.1 fees, the express Company convenience right, and limiting HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term should move together. Note that the cap measures against a revenue-share fee stream; if HDI resists, we can express it as three months' average Section 3 payments.
4. **Confirm the change-of-control position.** No change-of-control language appears anywhere, so HDI has no exit right today, but this remains unconfirmed — verify before finalising the Section 10.3 paragraph.
5. **Hold the exclusivity fallback in reserve.** If HDI will not accept express non-exclusivity, our fallback is a 12-month restriction limited to Deerskin Products with automatic termination on service level or delivery failure. Do not concede the exclusive right in the "Deerskin" brand.
6. **Insurance fallback:** E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M if HDI resists the preferred limits.
7. **No action required** on MFN, minimum commitments or non-solicitation. Preserve HDI's covenants in Sections 1.8 and 6.3 unchanged — both run in our favour."}
